name: walls-outdoor-palette
description:
Grayscale boilerplate of the outdoor `walls` autotile — the same 4x4 pieces, layout, gids and colliders, redrawn in the indoor boilerplate's flat palette, plus a ground row (gids 4197-4200) so a sample map can be drawn from this sheet alone.

FOUR COLOURS CARRY EVERYTHING. Dark #3A3A50 is outline. White #F8F8F8 is a wall's TOP, its cap, with a #E8E7ED lip on its last row. Sage #9CA99E is a wall's SOUTH-FACING SIDE, with its first row #8C9594 in the cap's shadow. Grey is ground: speckled outside a compound, paved inside.

Wall autotile — a nine-slice ring (rows 0-2) PLUS four step pieces (row 3) for turns the nine-slice cannot express.

The art is handed, and mixing handedness is what breaks a wall: every left-handed piece draws its cream stroke at x9-11 and every right-handed one at x5-7, 4px apart. A rectangle only ever needs one handedness per side, so nine pieces suffice; a stepped ring turns twice per step and needs a matching-handed piece for BOTH turns, which is what row 3 supplies.

Colliders follow the art, and the whole sheet is built from exactly TWO boxes. A horizontal band blocks a 6px strip at its base (y10-16) — which is also what makes it draw behind an entity standing above it. A vertical rail blocks the 5px column it is drawn on (x8-12 left-handed, x4-8 right-handed), full height, because a rail is crossed sideways and a short box would leave a hole between rows. Every corner and step piece is one or both of those, clipped to the columns its own art covers; nothing is full-cell.

So a band's 6px base is the ONE height in this sheet, north and south alike (walls-1-0 and walls-1-2 are pixel-identical), and it carries unbroken through every corner and step. A piece needs the rail box too only when its arm turns NORTH — the four pieces where it turns south sit above a vertical run that already seals that column, so they are a base strip and nothing more.

walls.description: 4x4 wall autotile: nine-slice ring plus four step pieces.

walls-0-0.name: top_left_wall_corner
walls-0-0.description: North-west corner. Its cream arm sits at x9-11, the same column every other left-handed piece uses, so a run above or below meets it exactly. Collider is the north run's 6px base strip, restricted to the half the art occupies (art starts at x8, y4) — the same box the run east of it uses, so the walk-behind strip carries straight through the corner instead of stopping a whole tile early. The arm turns SOUTH from here, and the west run below already blocks its column full height, so the 10px above the strip needs no collider: it only ever touches the outside.

walls-1-0.name: top_middle_wall_edge
walls-1-0.description: North wall run, repeat horizontally. The 6px collider at its base is also its depth baseline: an entity standing in the 10px above it is drawn behind the wall, one standing south of it in front. Both sides matter here — unlike a building, a wall encloses walkable floor (walls-1-1 is non-solid), so this tile is approachable from inside and out.

walls-2-0.name: top_right_wall_corner
walls-2-0.description: North-east corner. Right-handed: cream arm at x5-7. Mirror of the north-west corner, and its collider follows the same rule — the north run's 6px base strip over the half the art occupies.

walls-3-0.name: band_end_west
walls-3-0.description: End cap for a horizontal run. A band is drawn to CONTINUE, so its vertical edges carry no outline; a decorative run inside a room has to stop somewhere, and without a cap its two end cells leave raw fill against the world. Closes the WEST edge — use as the first cell of a run.

walls-0-1.name: middle_left_wall_edge
walls-0-1.description: West wall run, repeat vertically. Cream arm at x9-11, so the rail is x8-12 and the collider is exactly those 5 columns — the same box every left-handed arm in this sheet uses. It stays full height because a rail is crossed sideways: a short box would leave a hole between every pair of rows. The 3px east of it is inside the compound and the 8px west of it is outside, which is what makes a one-course wall read one tile thick without the collider claiming half a cell.

walls-1-1.name: wall_interior
walls-1-1.description: Empty interior cell. Nothing drawn or blocked — fill the enclosed area with a ground tile.

walls-2-1.name: middle_right_wall_edge
walls-2-1.description: East wall run, repeat vertically. Cream arm at x5-7, so the rail is x4-8 and the collider is exactly those 5 columns — mirror of the west run, and the same box every right-handed arm in this sheet uses. Full height for the same reason.

walls-3-1.name: band_end_east
walls-3-1.description: End cap for a horizontal run. A band is drawn to CONTINUE, so its vertical edges carry no outline; a decorative run inside a room has to stop somewhere, and without a cap its two end cells leave raw fill against the world. Closes the EAST edge — use as the last cell of a run.

walls-0-2.name: bottom_left_wall_corner
walls-0-2.description: South-west corner. Two boxes, for the same reason step_west_to_north needs two: the arm turns NORTH into the west run, so its 5px rail column (x8-12, exactly where the art is) blocks top to bottom, while the band it caps only blocks its 6px base strip. One box would be their bounding box — the full cell — which is what used to make this corner 10px taller than the run beside it and cap the compound's inner walk-behind strip a tile early. The arm is what seals that strip from the outside.

walls-1-2.name: bottom_middle_wall_edge
walls-1-2.description: South wall run, repeat horizontally. Pixel-identical to the north run — same outline at y4, same cream stroke at y5-7, same base outline at y15 — so it takes the same 6px base strip and is walk-behind on the same terms. A wall encloses walkable floor, so the 10px above this band is the INSIDE of the compound: an entity standing there is further from the camera than the band and is correctly drawn behind it.

walls-2-2.name: bottom_right_wall_corner
walls-2-2.description: South-east corner. Mirror of the south-west corner: band base strip plus the right-handed rail column (x4-8) at full height, since the arm turns NORTH into the east run.

walls-0-3.name: step_west_to_south
walls-0-3.description:
THE PIECES THE NINE-SLICE LACKS. A nine-slice has one corner per turn direction, each with its cream arm locked to one column. A stepped or curved wall turns TWICE in a row, so the second turn needs the same connection set with the arm on the OTHER column — without it the rail jumps 4px mid-wall and the run ends uncapped. Band arrives from the west and turns down, arm at x9-11 (left-handed).

Collider: the band's 6px base strip, stopping at x13 where the art does. The arm turns SOUTH, so the west run in the cell below already blocks its column — one box is the whole footprint, and the 10px above it stays walk-behind like the straight run it continues.

walls-1-3.name: step_west_to_north
walls-1-3.description:
THE PIECES THE NINE-SLICE LACKS. A nine-slice has one corner per turn direction, each with its cream arm locked to one column. A stepped or curved wall turns TWICE in a row, so the second turn needs the same connection set with the arm on the OTHER column — without it the rail jumps 4px mid-wall and the run ends uncapped. Band arrives from the west and turns up, arm at x9-11 (left-handed).

Collider: TWO boxes, because this footprint is an L and the bounding box of an L is the whole cell — which is both wider than the art and full height, cancelling the walk-behind the straight runs have. The band's 6px base strip, plus the arm's 5px column at full height because the arm continues NORTH and a vertical run blocks its column top to bottom.

walls-2-3.name: step_east_to_south
walls-2-3.description:
THE PIECES THE NINE-SLICE LACKS. A nine-slice has one corner per turn direction, each with its cream arm locked to one column. A stepped or curved wall turns TWICE in a row, so the second turn needs the same connection set with the arm on the OTHER column — without it the rail jumps 4px mid-wall and the run ends uncapped. Band arrives from the east and turns down, arm at x5-7 (right-handed).

Collider: mirror of step_west_to_south — the band's 6px base strip from x4, where the art starts. The arm turns SOUTH into an east run that already blocks its column.

walls-3-3.name: step_east_to_north
walls-3-3.description:
THE PIECES THE NINE-SLICE LACKS. A nine-slice has one corner per turn direction, each with its cream arm locked to one column. A stepped or curved wall turns TWICE in a row, so the second turn needs the same connection set with the arm on the OTHER column — without it the rail jumps 4px mid-wall and the run ends uncapped. Band arrives from the east and turns up, arm at x5-7 (right-handed).

Collider: mirror of step_west_to_north — two boxes, the band's base strip plus the arm's 5px column at full height, since the arm continues NORTH.

walls-0-4.name: ground_plain
walls-0-4.description: Outdoor ground, flat grey with a few flecks. The fill outside a compound. Walkable.

walls-1-4.name: ground_plain_alt
walls-1-4.description: Outdoor ground, same grey with its flecks moved, for breaking up a large area. Walkable.

walls-2-4.name: yard_paving
walls-2-4.description: Yard paving, light grey slabs with a grout seam on its north and west edges, so it tiles into a grid. The fill inside a compound. Walkable.

walls-3-4.name: yard_paving_worn
walls-3-4.description: Yard paving with one slab darker, for breaking up a large yard. Walkable.
